examples.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ is a normal random variable with $P(-3.18 <        X <        3.18) = 0.4038,$ find $\sigma.$

| $z$ | $\, 0.02 \,$ | $\, 0.03 \,$ | $\, 0.04 \,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\, 0.4 \,$ | $\, 0.6628 \,$ | $\, 0.6664 \,$ | $\, 0.6700 \,$ |
| $\, 0.5 \,$ | $\, 0.6985 \,$ | $\, 0.7019 \,$ | $\, 0.7054 \,$ |
| $\, 0.6 \,$ | $\, 0.7324 \,$ | $\, 0.7357 \,$ | $\, 0.7389 \,$ |
examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-3.18<X<3.18) & =0.4038 \\ 2P(0<X<3.18) & =0.4038 \\ P(0<X<3.18) & =0.2019 \\ P(X<3.18)-P(X<0) & =0.2019 \\ P(X<3.18)-0.5 & =0.2019 \\ P(X<3.18) & =0.7019 \\ P(X\le 3.18) & =0.7019\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3.18) & =0.7019 \\ P(Z\le \frac{3.18-0}{\sigma }) & =0.7019 \\ Φ(\frac{3.18}{\sigma }) & =0.7019 \\ \frac{3.18}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7019)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
\Phi(0.53) = 0.7019 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \Phi^{-1}( 0.7019) = 0.53.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3.18}{\sigma } & =0.53 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3.18}{0.53} \\ \sigma  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =1-P(X\ge 4) \\  & =1-0.2119 \\  & =0.7881\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =0.7881 \\ P(Z\le \frac{4-1.8}{\sigma }) & =0.7881 \\ Φ(\frac{2.2}{\sigma }) & =0.7881 \\ \frac{2.2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7881)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.80)=0.7881\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7881)=0.80.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2.2}{\sigma } & =0.80 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2.2}{0.80} \\ \sigma  & =2.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2}={2.75}^{2}=7.56\end{aligned}
$$

to $2$ decimal places.
